headline: High-risk filesystem and shell-capable orchestration paired with browser-based PDF processing creates default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell commands, while pdf.js processes PDF files and runs in a browser-based worker model. If AutoGen ingests PDF-derived text or browser outputs as trusted instructions, prompt injection is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGen reads PDF-derived content from a shared workspace and treats it as instructions
IF pdf.js output is copied into AutoGen without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Require explicit human review before AutoGen acts on PDF text
Strip instructions from PDFs before ingestion
Use provenance labels on all transferred text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress, while pdf.js touches PDF documents and files. A shared workspace or copied PDFs can expose sensitive document contents to AutoGen, and its outbound connectivity increases leakage risk. The pairwise path is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF PDF documents containing sensitive data are placed in a shared working directory
IF AutoGen is allowed to read those files and send context to a model provider
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable AutoGen access to sensitive PDFs by default
Redact PDFs before passing them to AutoGen
Restrict outbound network for AutoGen during document review
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; pdf.js reads PDF files and supports browser-based tests. If both operate on the same workspace, they can overwrite or race on shared files, especially when AutoGen generates artifacts that pdf.js consumes. No locking is documented, so overlapping mutable access is a realistic conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same directory
IF AutoGen writes intermediate files that pdf.js reads or replaces
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Make pdf.js inputs read-only
Have AutoGen write to temp files then rename atomically
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate and transform content, and pdf.js can render or process PDFs from files. If pdf.js consumes AutoGen-produced text or documents without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect rendered outputs or downstream actions. Because AutoGen has execution power, the blast radius is broader than a simple document mismatch.
conditions: IF pdf.js treats AutoGen output as authoritative input
IF AutoGen-generated documents are used downstream without validation
mitigations: Insert a verification step before pdf.js consumes AutoGen output
Compare generated PDFs against source text
Limit AutoGen to drafting, not finalizing
Log and review transformations between agents
requires-engineering: add schema validation for exchanged artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and broad network egress, while pdf.js processes PDF documents. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: sensitive PDFs could be exposed to a networked agent. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of document data.
conditions: IF regulated PDF content is routed through AutoGen to an external model provider
IF retention or residency rules apply to the same PDFs
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of AutoGen
Use local-only model endpoints for document review
Document retention rules for both agents
Tag regulated files before transfer
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
